name: Tidewater Hall
description:
Tidewater Hall sits on the edge of Circuit District 14, occupying a building that has been continuously operating as a gathering space since 2147 — one of the oldest standing venues in GLMZ. Originally a water reclamation cooperative office, it was converted by a group of pipe workers and their families into a dance hall after the Second Grid Expansion displaced their neighborhood. The main floor holds four hundred comfortably, with a raised stage at the north end backed by original corrugated steel walls that the current management has never seen fit to replace, arguing the acoustics are unimprovable. A secondary room in the basement — known as the Cellar — hosts smaller acoustic sets for crowds of sixty or eighty.

Tidewater is community-owned through a cooperative share structure; any Circuit resident can buy a share for Φ50, and shareholders vote on programming, pricing, and policy. Drinks are priced at Circuit wages. The hall runs six nights a week, hosting everything from the large-format drone and polyrhythm dance nights that have made it a Circuit institution to the quieter acoustic sessions where elder musicians teach the traditional forms — Yoruba percussion patterns, Nordic drone harmonics, Andean wind structures — not as ethnic artifacts but as living techniques available to anyone who wants to learn them. The Olufemi-Strand Collective recorded their album Common Ground here in 2219.
creator: various
genre: Circuit folk, polyrhythmic dance, acoustic drift, worker ballads
audience: Circuit workers, cooperative members, families, off-duty technicians, the occasional Tier 3 resident seeking something real
cultural_impact: Tidewater Hall is one of the few venues in GLMZ that has resisted every acquisition attempt by Vantablack Media and its subsidiaries, citing its cooperative ownership structure as a legal barrier. This has made it a model studied by community organizers across the city. Its weekly open sessions have produced a disproportionate number of musicians who went on to significant careers, and its cooperative model has been replicated — with varying success — in four other Circuit districts. The hall's physical bulletin board, a genuine analog corkboard, is considered the most reliable source of Circuit neighborhood news in District 14.
story_hooks: Vantablack Media has found a legal mechanism to challenge the cooperative's ownership structure, and the shareholders have one week to mount a defense — they need someone who understands both corporate law and how to disappear a paper trail.

A musician playing a quiet set in the Cellar performs a song that contains, encoded in its rhythm structure, a message meant for someone specific in the audience — someone who hasn't been seen publicly in two years.

The hall's original founding documents, stored in a waterproof case beneath the stage, contain the names of people who were supposed to be dead by 2147, and a map to something buried under Circuit District 14.
